requirements.description: Casino War compares one player card with one dealer card from a six-deck shoe, offers surrender or war on an initial tie, and awards a second war tie to the player.
requirements.notes: Allocated by GitHub issue #77 for issue #82; deterministic engine tests cover initial wins, losses, ties, surrender, war wins, war losses, and player-favoring second ties.

requirements.description: Authenticated sessions own isolated reload-safe Casino War state, tie decisions, recent rounds, and canonical route restoration.
requirements.notes: Normal-user session bindings override caller-supplied player ids, and persisted settled rounds survive backend restart.

requirements.description: Casino War ante, optional war wager, surrender return, and settlement movements use the shared ledger exactly once under stable action identifiers.
requirements.notes: Game code never mutates balances directly; replay proof matches stable Casino War action ids and verifies complete required versus committed movements.

requirements.description: The Casino War surface provides complete English and Russian copy and remains usable without overflow across required desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.
requirements.notes: Acceptance evidence covers both locales, all four named viewports, initial and war-result states, and canonical route restoration.

requirements.description: Catalog, contract, browser, and long-suite discovery automatically include Casino War with requirement, module, version, and visual evidence traceability.
requirements.notes: The descriptor uses sort order 80 and the normalized tests.game_drivers.casino_war:play driver reference reserved by issue #77.

requirements.description: Casino War records committed ledger-intent markers and the terminal settled phase through the shared provider-owned atomic player game-state helper, so competing server processes preserve both transitions instead of publishing stale complete documents.
requirements.notes: The first #704 slice migrated money-adjacent reconciliation publications; issue #771 retains those atomic markers and terminal transitions while retiring the remaining direct preparation and rollback saves. The v1 route and response envelope remain unchanged.

requirements.description: Casino War prepares initial rounds and tie decisions through the shared provider-owned atomic player game-state helper, detects duplicate action identifiers inside the same cross-process boundary, and compensates only an exact action-owned preparation after authoritative ledger absence while preserving sibling state and bounded history.
requirements.notes: Real JSON-provider process races prove preparation preserves sibling updates and same-action contenders consume one round or decision. Deterministic failures restore exact action-owned cards, requests, rounds, and pruned history only when the first new ledger action is absent; a committed lost response remains prepared for exactly-once recovery. State and money still use separate provider boundaries, so a second production worker remains blocked under parent issue #704.
